speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The Singapore economy is going through its most severe downturn since independence.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) seeks to anchor economic and financial stability, and support businesses and individuals in riding out the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS is also positioning the financial sector to emerge stronger, so that it can continue to support the economy and provide more good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS has adopted an accommodative monetary stance, to complement the Government's significant fiscal policy measures in mitigating the economic impact of the COVID-19 Circuit Breaker and broad-based decline in global demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Through its money market operations, MAS has and will continue to ensure the smooth functioning of funding markets in Singapore, so that there is no disruption to banks' ability to continue to extend credit to the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Sustaining the safety and soundness of our financial sector is critical for supporting the economy through the downturn as well as its recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Banks and insurance companies generally entered the crisis with financially strong balance sheets.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS' stress tests found them to be resilient in a deep downturn.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Singapore's financial sector has also demonstrated strong operational resilience and has been able to continue to serve customers through the different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: This has reflected years of investments in digitalisation, sound business continuity planning and agile adjustments to work processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: To ensure that financial institutions stay resilient financially and operationally, MAS has provided a number of regulatory reliefs that do not compromise prudential standards, and will continue to supervise the industry closely.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS and the financial industry introduced a comprehensive package of measures that have provided relief to individuals and businesses in meeting their loan and insurance commitments, and helped ensure continued access to bank credit and insurance coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: As the measures provided temporary relief and come with longer term costs, they need to be gradually withdrawn.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS is working closely with the industry to ensure a well-paced exit that minimises sharp cliff effects for borrowers, while safeguarding financial stability.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The financial sector remains integral to Singapore's recovery from the COVID-19 crisis and longer term growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS will work with the industry to ensure that the financial sector is well-equipped with the skills and capabilities to emerge stronger from the crisis, and advance Singapore as a global financial centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The financial sector is on track to meeting its targets for both growth and job creation that were set out in our 5-year Industry Transformation Map for 2016 – 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS takes a comprehensive approach, working closely with tripartite partners to support the reskilling and upskilling of the local workforce, and create jobs and traineeship opportunities in the financial sector for fresh graduates and mid-career workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: We are also working with major financial institutions (FIs) to ensure a solid Singaporean core in their workforces, complemented by diverse and high quality manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: These efforts include developing a strong pipeline of Singaporeans for senior responsibilities in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The package will enable structured talent development programmes for more than 900 Singaporeans among those newly hired by FIs over the next three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: FIs have also committed to hire significant numbers under the various SGUnited Jobs & Skills programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: To prepare local mid-career workers for new or transformed roles, MAS is working closely with the Institute of Banking and Finance and Workforce Singapore to train and redeploy workers into financial institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: For example, more than 200 attachments have been offered by 18 FIs this year under the Technology in Finance Immersion Programme, in growth areas such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and data analytics.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Following five years of investments in digital transformation and innovation by financial sector players, Singapore is now widely regarded as one of the top FinTech hubs globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: An estimated 1,000 FinTech firms are based here.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The Singapore FinTech Festival and Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology later this year will deliver the world's first week-long round-the-clock, hybrid digital and physical event for attendees across the world, and will bring together the global innovation community despite the current travel constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: With the accelerated pace of digitalisation due to COVID-19, MAS is also working actively with other government agencies and the industry to drive further progress on electronic payments and digital banking.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: In addition, MAS will work with the financial services and FinTech sectors to adopt digital solutions that will strengthen operational resilience, improve productivity, better manage risks, as well as engage customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Achieving a high degree of digitalisation will be a key source of competitive advantage for our financial sector in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: Safeguarding the environment and managing climate-related risks is an increasingly important issue both globally and in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: The financial sector plays a critical role in supporting Singapore through the downturn as well as its recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
text: MAS is working closely with the financial services and FinTech sectors to achieve these aims and help Singapore emerge stronger from the crisis.
